reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the November 5 close: SPX 7,353.73, down 6.26% from its 120-day high, 4.33% below its 50-day and just 0.42% above its 200-day; SMH 447.73, down 33.36% from its high and below Zone 2 ($470-505), while NVDA 181.60 sits inside Zone 2 ($175-185); VIX closed 28.18, up 69.66% on the day, with high-yield OAS 3.32 calm and the mechanical capitulation tally at 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: A daily close above the SPX 7,750-7,820 failure zone with SMH reclaiming $505 and VIX under 20 would prove the correction read wrong and void this ladder; conversely a sustained credit break (high-yield OAS above 4.0) voids the Watch stance toward full stand-down.

ladder.response: No new probes; hold cash in bills and wait for a second-low structure — the correction is deepening, not offering a buying opportunity.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below its 200-day at 7,322.74, or SMH closes below $440

ladder.response: Treat as a sell-the-rally zone, not a re-entry; no adds into the failure zone until a close above it with VIX under 20.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone, or SMH rallies toward 580-600 and stalls

ladder.response: Full stand-down: no probes of any kind; the correction has become a credit event and this ladder is void.
ladder.trigger: VIX closes above 30, or high-yield OAS breaks above 4.0

ladder.response: Re-arm the Tranche A probe on the ladder's terms — starter size only, limit at the zone top.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes back inside Zone 2 ($470-505) with VIX back under 25 and the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better

reaction.trapRisk: November 5 was the washout, not the confirmation: SMH volume ran 2.85x its 20-day average but closed in the bottom 6% of its range — no climax reversal — and VIX closed at its 5-day high, not rolling over. The first bounce is the trap: a gap-up open that stalls into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone is a pivot-and-fail setup, so do not chase the first bounce; entries wait for the failed bounce and a second low that holds.

strategyPosture: Watch. The VIX closed at 28.18, above the 25 stand-down line, SMH at $447.73 is below Zone 2 which voided the prior Tranche A arm, and the mechanical tally is 2 of 4 with no climax reversal and no VIX rollover — so there is no probe until a fresh Zone 2 print plus a tally of 3 of 4 or better and the VIX back under 25. Cash stays in bills; the work today is watching the second low form, not chasing the first bounce.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking, not dismissing: credit conditions can flip, and a rotation that keeps widening eventually becomes the rollover. If the gap keeps growing while lending standards tighten, the rotation read fails. For now the data and the narrative agree — this is concentrated weakness, not systemic stress.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names sit 18.07% below their 52-week highs on average against 6.2% for SPY — an 11.87-point divergence gap — with Apple the strongest at 3.2% below its high and Tesla the weakest at 31.1% below. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), and SPX itself is only 6.26% off its 120-day high and still 0.42% above its 200-day (7,322.74).
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — Mag7 unwinds while the index holds
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a leadership rotation, not a broad market rollover: the index is down but not broken, while the handful of names that dominate it by weight are being sold hard.
themes.watchFor: Mag7-vs-SPY divergence gap widening past 15 points, or SLOOS moving out of the LOOSE zone.

themes.counterRead: Oversold is not a bottom and growing revenue is not a floor: multiples can keep compressing (Applied Materials and KLAC already show MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION as the decline reason), and SMH at $447.73 is already BELOW Zone 2 ($470-505), which voided the prior Tranche A arm. The opportunity is real but the timing signal has not fired — the data says buy the zone, the tape says the zone just broke.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue data has not broken. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year while the stock sits 25.4% below its high at $181.60 (RSI 25.4) inside Zone 2 ($175-185). Broadcom revenue is up 55% with a 67.8% gross margin and 42.1% free-cash-flow margin while 41.1% below its high. Of 36 tracked dislocations, the dominant decline reason is SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not fundamental: Datadog revenue up 27.7-34.4% at 41.9% below its high, Snowflake up 34.3% at 29.9% below, Cloudflare up 36.4% at 34% below. RSI readings across the complex run 22-35 — deeply oversold on intact growth.
themes.label: AI infrastructure washout — fundamentals still growing, prices collapsed
themes.narrative: The market is pricing the AI buildout as finished: semis and the AI supply chain have been sold as if demand is breaking, with SMH down 33.36% from its high and 11.21% in a single day.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing back inside Zone 2 ($470-505) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better.

themes.counterRead: The narrative has run ahead of the evidence: no demand print in the data shows a buildout halt, and the dislocation table tags these declines SENTIMENT_DRIVEN. But the risk is not imaginary — the Texas vote is a real policy event, and if today's Vistra report confirms a demand or permitting hit, the narrative becomes the data. Until then, treat the election repricing as a fear trade to verify, not a verdict to act on.
themes.dataAnchor: The price moves are large and fast: TSMC down 10%, UMC down 16%, ASML down 8% in the post-election chip rout; Vistra fell 14% on the Texas election vote and sits 42.6% below its 52-week high at $112.89, down 28.14% in a month. Against that, Vistra revenue is growing 19.1% year over year, the stock trades at 2.2x sales, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. Vistra reports today, November 6 — the print is what settles whether the policy story has a demand leg.
themes.label: Election shock — chips and power repriced on policy risk
themes.narrative: The post-midterm story is that election results reprice the AI buildout itself: chip names routed on the Democrats' wins and power names sold on the Texas vote, as if policy now caps the data-center buildout.
themes.watchFor: Vistra's November 6 report — guidance on data-center demand and Texas exposure.

themes.counterRead: Credit calm is a necessary condition for a bottom, not a sufficient one: VIX above 25 already trips the stand-down, and a fear spike this sharp can force selling (margin, de-grossing) even with funding intact. If high-yield spreads break above 4.0, the correction becomes a credit event and every ladder rung below is void. Watch credit, not just the VIX print.
themes.dataAnchor: High-yield option-adjusted spread is 3.32, calm and not cracking, well below the 4.0 stand-down line. The 2s10s curve is +0.32 (not inverted), the 10-year is 4.90% with a 2.66% real yield, and the Fed funds rate is 3.88%. The mechanical tally confirms the split: credit-calm is confirmed, while the VIX-rollover signal is not (VIX at its 5-day high, not rolling over) and the volume-climax-reversal signal is not (SMH volume 2.85x its 20-day average but the close in the bottom 6% of its range).
themes.label: Credit calm while equities panic
themes.narrative: Equities are panicking — VIX closed at 28.18, up 69.66% on the day — while credit is not confirming a funding event. The fear is in stocks, not in the funding channel.
themes.watchFor: High-yield OAS crossing 4.0, or VIX closing back under 25.

whereWaveBuilds: In the AI complex. SMH is already below Zone 2 and NVDA sits inside it at $181.60, so the next move is decided by whether SPX holds its 200-day at 7,322.74 (only 0.42% above the close) and whether the first bounce fails and a second low holds — or breaks lower.
